in_arabic.name: نجد
in_arabic.meaning: الارتفاع و العلو و المكان المرتفع
in_arabic.long_meaning: نجد هو الارتفاع و العلو و المكان المرتفع، و يطلق على منطقة في شبه الجزيرة العربية تشتهر بعلوها و جبالها. و في القرآن الكريم، ذُكرت كلمة نجد في سورة البلد: 'أَتَعْلَمُ مَن هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنكَ نَجْدًا'، أي أكثر ارتفاعًا و علوًا. و يعتبر اسم نجد ذا أهمية كبيرة في الثقافة الإسلامية، حيث يرتبط بالارتفاع و العز و الشرف.

in_urdu.name: نجد
in_urdu.long_meaning: نجد کا مطلب اونچائی، بلندی، اور بلند مقام سے ہے۔ یہ نام عربی زبان کی جڑوں سے ماخوذ ہے، جہاں 'ن-ج-د' جڑ کا مطلب ہے 'اونچا کرنا' یا 'بلند کرنا'۔ اسلامی تقویم میں، نجد ایک ایسا خطہ ہے جو جزیرہ نما عرب میں واقع ہے اور اپنی بلندیوں اور جبال کے لئے جانا جاتا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلم معاشرے میں، یہ نام بچوں کو عزت، شان، اور بلند مقام کی دعا کے ساتھ منسوب کیا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: नजद
in_hindi.long_meaning: नजद नाम का अर्थ ऊंचाई, उच्च स्थान, और श्रेष्ठता है। यह नाम अरबी भाषा की जड़ों से लिया गया है, जहां 'न-ज-द' मूल का अर्थ है 'ऊंचा करना' या 'उन्नति करना'। इस्लामी परंपरा में, नजद एक ऐसा क्षेत्र है जो अरब प्रायद्वीप में स्थित है और अपनी ऊंचाइयों और पहाड़ों के लिए प्रसिद्ध है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम बच्चों को सम्मान, प्रतिष्ठा, और उच्च दर्जे की कामना के साथ दिया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: نجد
in_pashto.long_meaning: نجد د لوړوالی، بلندی، او لوی مقام معنی لري. دا نوم د عربي ژبې له ريښو څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چیرته چې 'ن-ج-د' ريښې معنی یې 'لوړ کړل' یا 'بلند کړل' دی. په اسلامي دود کې، نجد يو داسې سيمه ده چې په عربي ټاپووزمه کې موقع لري او د خپلو لوړوالیو او غرونو لپاره پيژندل کيږي. د افغان او پښتنو په دود، دا نوم ماشومانو ته د عزت، شهرت، او لوړ مقام دعا سره ورکول کيږي.

in_english.name: Najd
in_english.long_meaning: The name Najd originates from Arabic roots, where 'n-j-d' means 'to elevate' or 'to rise'. In Islamic tradition, Najd refers to a region in the Arabian Peninsula known for its elevated terrain. The name symbolizes exaltation, nobility, and high status. Historically, it has been used to signify places of spiritual elevation and enlightenment. In modern usage across Muslim cultures, Najd is given to children as a blessing for a life of honor, distinction, and elevated status.

data.cultural_impact: The name Najd holds historical importance, as it was the heartland of the Arabian Peninsula in pre-Islamic times. It was also the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), who hailed from the town of Mecca. Najd has also been a significant center of Bedouin Arab culture, with its vast deserts and camel herding traditions. Further, Najd has been the home to various Islamic spiritual movements and rituals, such as the annual gathering at the Prophet's Well near Al-Munafah.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, Najd is considered a sacred and spiritual place. It was in Najd where the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) received his first revelations from Allah, marking the beginning of the Islamic faith. Additionally, Najd has a strong association with Sufism, the mystical branch of Islam, as many Sufis have sought refuge and isolation in the deserts of Najd to pursue their spiritual practices. Furthermore, Najd is believed to be rich in spiritual energy due to its connection with the early Islamic community and the many religious sites and practices located there, making it a popular destination for pilgrims seeking spiritual growth and renewal.

historical_references.reference: Najd was a major center of Arabian tribal confederations and the homeland of the early Islamic state under Muhammad and the Rashidun Caliphs. It was the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad and the site of several significant early Islamic battles, such as the Battle of Hunayn and the Battle of Ta'if.

Najd was also a prosperous region during the Ottoman Empire, with significant agricultural and commercial activities, especially in the areas of dates, grains, and livestock. It was an important center of Islamic scholarship and learning, with numerous madrasas and mosques.
historical_references.context: Ottoman Empire, Islamic education and culture, Arabian Peninsula

modern_usage.modern_context: The region of Najd, historically located in present-day Saudi Arabia, has emerged as a significant economic powerhouse, technological hub, and a place of religious significance in the contemporary Middle East. It is home to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, which has the second-largest proven oil reserves in the world. The region's wealth has facilitated the development of advanced infrastructure, including world-class cities, universities, and research institutions. In addition to its economic prowess, Najd is a focal point for religious tourism, with sites such as the Al-Masjid an-Nabawi (The Prophet's Mosque) in Medina and the Al-Masjid al-Haram (The Grand Mosque) in Mecca attracting millions of pilgrims annually. The United Arab Emirates and Qatar, two other countries in the region, have also experienced rapid economic growth and are investing heavily in technology and innovation. The modern context of Najd reflects its role as an essential economic, technological, and religious center in the Middle East.
